title: Centered Title and Author Headings

illustrates.quote: Do not insert a blank line between connected headings.

blocks.features: Story title; large stylized red cursive script logo/graphic (book-cover title treatment), centered, spanning two print lines.
Author byline directly beneath the title graphic; small italic serif type, right-aligned in print.

print.notes: Two connected headings (title + author) with no blank line between them in braille, per rule 4.3.3, even though the print title is a decorative script logotype and the author name is a small right-aligned byline rather than a second display heading.
print.printFeatures: Boxed cover/title-page excerpt; title in large decorative red script font/graphic, author name in small italic serif beneath it, right-aligned.

braille.notes: Line 1 blank; line 2 the centered title heading; line 3 an all-blank-cell row (see uncertain); line 4 the centered byline heading, directly beneath with no intervening blank line per 4.3.3; line 5 blank.

uncertain: Line 3 (an all-blank braille row between the two headings) is preserved verbatim as "" per the transcribe-exactly convention; it is most likely an unused wrapped-title continuation slot (the title happened to fit on one line) rather than a rule violation, but this reading is inference, not something the rule text states outright.
resolution: Both runs' braille.lines agree (independently re-verified against .txt lines 3204-3208, confirming margin=8). The one substantive disagreement was `print.blocks[1].level`: run A said 1 (centered), run B said 2 (cell-5). Resolved in favour of A: both braille lines carry the SAME 11-cell leading indent, and 11 matches the centering formula (40-len)/2 for both texts exactly (len 17 each) -- neither line has the fixed 4-cell or 6-cell indent of a cell-5/cell-7 heading, so both are centered, level 1. Run B's level 2 for the byline is a transcription error, contradicted by its own braille data.
